FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (Second Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized 
by the Paints, Varnishes and Related Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division 
Council. 


This Indian standard was first published in 1952 on full alignment with JSS 3055 ‘Specification for Black Japan’, 
issued by the Department of Standardization, Ministry of Defence, Government of India. 


The material, commercially known as Black Japan. Black Japans constitute a class of general purposes, fast 
drying, bituminous base paints. The utility of the material depends largely on the ingredients used in their 
manufacture. Black japans are expected to be free from foreign matter, sediments and undissolved water. Depending 
upon the applications, three types of Black Japan are widely used. They are namely Type A, Type B and Type C. 


This standard was first revised in 1973 amalgamating IS 341 : 1952, IS 1257 : 1958 and IS 1704 : 1960. In the 
first revision the requirement for ash content for Types B and C of the material had been specified. For Black 
Japan Type C, a requirement for force-drying time of 1 h at 100 to 105?C in scratch hardness test, and a rate of 
heating in the test for resistance to heat had been prescribed. For Type A of the material, the test for resistance to 
kerosene has been dropped which was found not necessary by the concerned Technical Committee as the material 
is required to pass the test for reaction with white paint and varnishes which are having relatively more aromatic 
content which may penetrate more in bitumen than kerosene. 


Revision of this standard has been taken up with a view to incorporate the maximum permissible limit of lead as 
lead restriction clause in this standard. The Technical Committee responsible for the formulation of this standard 
observed that in general some paints like this paint are used for household/decorative as well as for industrial 
applications. Taking cognizance of the fact that lead exposure of human being, particularly children, has adverse 
effect on human health and also adverse impact on environment and safety, the Technical Committee felt the need 
to introduce different levels of lead restriction in all paint standards likely to be used for household and decorative 
applications. It was also decided to introduce lead restriction in some of the industrial paints, as far as possible, 
keeping in view relevance of lead restriction with respect to application condition and service life of the paint and 
wherever the product corresponding to a particular specification 1s of such composition that it would be easy to 
incorporate lead restriction without creating any negative impact. 


This product 1s extensively used for painting of grill, gates, metal roof etc, in house and buildings. 


The Technical Committee responsible for the formulation of this standard observed that technologically it is 
feasible to manufacture this product with low limit of lead. Therefore, the Committee felt that though in practice 
this paint is used for industrial coating applications, there is scope for prescribing maximum permissible low limit 
of lead to avoid hazardous impact of lead exposure to consumers and consequent adverse impact on environment 
and human health. Therefore, in this revision, lead restriction up to a maximum permissible limit of 300 ppm has 
been prescribed keeping in view of the scope for application of this paint in houses also and exposure to children 
to the paint once dried. Further, majority of consumers are not aware of the consequences of lead toxicity and its 
long-term implications to human health. Therefore, in this revision, alongwith lead restriction, a suitable cautionary 
notice has been included in the marking clause. 


Reference has been given to various Parts/Sections of IS 101 for testing the requirements given in the standard 
substituting reference to IS 197 : 1952 ‘Methods of test for varnishes and lacquers’ (since withdrawn). In this 
revision the present method of test for Accelerated weathering test which is by carbon arc type weathering apparatus 
has been substituted by a method using UV condensation type weathering apparatus as it is found that carbon arc 
type weathering apparatus are no more in use. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard 1s complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result ofa test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 
‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised). The number of significant places retained in the rounded off 
value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 341 : 2016 


Indian Standard 
BLACK JAPAN, TYPES A, B AND C — SPECIFICATION 


( Second Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements and 
methods of sampling and test for Black Japans, Types 
A, B and C. 


1.1.1 It 1s primarily suitable for application by 
brushing. Besides the applications as given in 4.1, this 
material can be used for painting of grill, gates, metal 
roof etc in houses and buildings. 


2 REFERENCES 


The standards listed in Annex A contain provisions 
which through reference in this text, constitute 
provisions of and necessary adjuncts to this standard. 
At the time of publication, the editions indicated were 
valid. All standards are subject to revision and parties 
to agreements based on this standard are encouraged 
to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent 
editions of the standards indicated in Annex A. 


3 TERMINOLOGY 


3.1 For the purpose of this standard, the definitions 
given in IS 1303 and the following shall apply. 


3.1.1 Registered Sample — Sample supplied in 
advance by a prospective supplier and registered by 
the approved testing authorities after testing it to all 
the requirements of this standard. A complete record 
of its performance shall be kept in respect of all tests. 


3.1.2. Approved Sample — The sample accepted by the 
indentor or inspection authority as the basis for the 
supply. When a sample tested and approved by the 
purchaser or inspection authority, the result of such tests 
as permits the supplier to meet the limits imposed by 
the specification for deliveries shall be made available 
to the supplier. 


4 TYPES 


4.1 Depending upon the applications the material shall 
have following three types: 


a) Type A — This material is used for the 
protection and decoration of metal and wood 
surfaces likely to be marked with white paint 
or finished with varnish. 

b) TypeB — This material commercially known 
as Black Japan B is meant for exterior use and 


intended for protection and decoration of 
undergear, coal bunks and platforms of 
locomotives and under frames of carriages 
besides other general utility as an outdoor 
finish. 

c) Type C — This material is durable and heat- 
resisting and is especially suitable for 
application for protection and decoration on 
surfaces which become hot under service 
conditions, such as those of locomotive and 
for other general purposes where a heat 
resisting finish is required. 


5 REQUIREMENTS 


5.1 Composition 


The materials shall be based on bituminous substances, 
such as gilsonite, drying oils, resins, driers and thinners 
in suitable proportions to satisfy the requirements of 
this standard. Carbon black conforming to IS 40 to the 
extent of one percent may be used as opacifier. The 
cashewnut shell liquid conforming to IS 840 which is 
rich in phenolic compounds is recommended in the 
manufacturing of black japan, Types B and C. 


5.2 Reaction with White Paint 


A film of the materials of all the three types when 
prepared and tested separately with white paint as 
prescribed in Annex B shall not show any discolouration 
of the coat of white paint. 


5.3 Reaction with Varnish, Exterior 


A film of the materials of Types A and B prepared 
separately and tested with varnish, exterior, as prescribed 
in Annex C, shall not produce green colouration of the 
varnish film when viewed in direct sunlight. 


5.4 Lead Restriction 


5.4.1 The material shall not contain lead or compounds 
of lead or mixtures of both, calculated as metallic lead 
more than 300 ppm, when tested for restriction from 
lead in accordance with IS 101 (Part 8/Sec 5). 


5.5 Durability 


This test is required for Types B and C of the material 
only. 


IS 341 : 2016 


5.5.1 Registered Sample 


5.5.1.1 A film of the material prepared from the 
registered sample as described under D-2 and D-3 and 
tested as prescribed under D-4 shall not break down in 
less than nine months. 


5.5.1.2 A film of the material shall be prepared from 
the registered sample and tested simultaneously as 
prescribed under D-4 in an accelerated weathering 
apparatus (UV condensation type). The film shall be 
examined daily for a period not exceeding 15 days and 
a complete record of performance maintained. 


5.5.2. Sample from Bulk Supply 


A film of the material prepared from a representative 
sample from bulk supply as described under D-2 
and D-3 and tested in the accelerated weathering 
apparatus as given under D-4. The film shall not be 
materially different in performance as compared with 
the record of the film of the registered sample when 
examined daily for a period of 15 days provided it does 
not fail earlier. 


5.6 The material shall also comply with the 
requirements given in Table 1. 


6 PACKING AND MARKING 


6.1 Packing 


Unless otherwise agreed to between the purchaser and 
the supplier, the material shall be packed as prescribed 
in IS 5661. The packing is subject to the provisions of 
the law in force in the country at that time. 


6.2 Marking 


6.2.1 Each container shall be marked with the 
following: 


a) Name ofthe material; 
b) Indication ofthe source of manufacture; 
c) Lead content, Max; 
d) Volume of the material; 
e) Batch No. or Lot No. in code or otherwise; 
f) Month and year of manufacture; and 
g) Type of the material 
h) A cautionary note as below 
1) Keep out of reach of children. 


2) Dried film of this paint may be harmful if 
eaten or chewed.

The container may also be marked with the Standard 
Mark. 


6.2.2.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by 
the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 
1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. 
The details of conditions under which the licence for 
the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to 
manufacturers or producers maybe obtained from the 
Bureau of Indian Standards. 


7 SAMPLING 


7.1 Preparation of Test Samples 
7.1.1 For Registration 


The sample shall be submitted in three different 
containers each containing not less than 500 ml of the 
material. 


7.1.1.1 As testing to the requirements for Types B and 
C of this standard covers a period of more than 
6 months, the supplier is advised to submit samples for 
registration sufficiently in advance within the period 
from October to December of the year, so that outdoor 
exposure test can be started during the period stipulated 
in D-3.3. 


7.1.2 Tender Sample 


The supplier may dispense with sending a tender sample 
provided that he declares that the material for which 
the tender is given is of the same quality as the sample 
previously registered in his name. 


7.1.3 Bulk Supply Sample 


Representative samples of the material shall be drawn 
as prescribed in IS 101 (Part 1/Sec 1). 


7.1.4 For Drying Time 


Prepare mild steel panel of sizes 150 mm x 100 mm x 
1.25 mm as prescribed in 2 of IS 101 (Part 1/Sec 3). 
Apply the paint uniformly on each side ofthe panel by 
brushing to give a dry film mass of 17 to 22 g/m? in 


IS 341 : 2016 


accordance with 101(Part 3/Sec 4). Prepared test panel 
then subjected to the test as specified in IS 101 (Part 3/ 
Sec 1) as soon as possible. 


7.1.5 For Flexibility and Adhesion Test 


For both bend test and scratch hardness test prepare 
separate burnished tin plate panels, rectangular, of sizes 
100 mm x 50 mm x 0.3 mm as prescribed in 3 of IS 101 
(Part 1/Sec 3). Apply one coat of material by brushing 
uniformly on the panels as to give a dry film mass of 
17 to 22 g/m? in accordance with IS 101(Part 3/Sec 4). 


7.1.5.1 For types Aand B 


The coated test panels shall be dried for 48 h and then 
shall be conditioned at a temperature of 27? + 2°C and 
relative humidity of 65 + 5 percent for a minimum time 
of 16 h. Prepared test panels then subjected to the test 
as prescribed in 2 and 3 of IS 101 (Part 5/Sec 2) for 
bend test and scratch hardness test respectively. 


7.1.5.2. For type C 


The coated test panel shall be force-dried at 100 to 
105?C for 1 h after 24 h of air-drying and cooled for 
further 24 h at room temperature before subjected to 
the test as prescribed in 2 and 3 of IS 101(Part 5/Sec 2) 
for bend test and scratch hardness test respectively. 


7.2 Criteria for Conformity 


A lot shall be declared as conforming to the 
requirements of this standard if the test results of the 
composite samples satisfy the requirements as 
prescribed in 5. 


8 TEST METHODS 

8.1 Tests shall be conducted as prescribed in 5.1 to 5.5 
and the methods referred in col 6 and 7 of Table 1. 
8.2 Quality of Reagents 


Unless specified otherwise ‘pure chemicals and distilled 
water' (see 1S 1070) shall be employed in tests. 


NOTE — ‘Pure chemicals’ shall mean chemicals that do not 
contain impurities which affect the results of analysis. 


8.3 Comparison with the performance of the registered 
sample shall be carried out.on the basis of the records 
maintained for the registered sample (see 5.5.1).

ANNEX B 


( Clause 5.2 ) 
DETERMINATION OF REACTION WITH WHITE PAINT 


B-0 OUTLINE OF THE METHOD 


B-0.1 A coat of white paint is applied on a panel coated 
with Black Japan after drying for a specific period and 
examined from any discolouration of the top coat. 


B-1 PREPARATION OF TEST PANELS 


B-1.1 Prepare a mild steel panel as described 
in 7.1.4. 


B-2 PROCEDURE 


B-2.1 Allow the panel to air-dry for 48 h. Apply 
uniformly a coat of the ready mixed paint, white 
coloured, conforming to IS 13607 over the film of the 
material of the panel and allow to dry for 24 h. 


B-3 OBSERVATIONS 


B-3.1 Examine the panel after the above period. The 
material shall be deemed to have passed the test when 
there shall be no discolouration of the coat of white 
paint. 


IS 341 : 2016 


ANNEX C 
(Clause 5.2) 
DETERMINATION OF REACTION WITH VARNISH, EXTERIOR 


C-0 OUTLINE OF THE METHOD 


C-0.1 A coat of varnish is applied on a panel coated 
with Black Japan after drying for a specific period and 
examined from any green colouration of the top coat. 


C-1 PREPARATION OF TEST PANELS 
C-1.1 Prepare a mild steel panel as described in 7.1.4. 


C-2 PROCEDURE 
C-2.1 Allow the panel to air-dry for 48 h. Apply 


uniformly a coat of the varnish, finishing, exterior 
conforming to IS 524 over the film of the material of 
the panel and allow to dry for 24 h. 


C-3 OBSERVATIONS 


C-3.1 Examine the panel after the above period. The 
material shall be deemed to have passed the test when 
there shall be no green colouration when the varnish 
film is viewed in direct sunlight. 


ANNEX D 
( Clauses 5.5.1.1, 5.5.1.2 and 5.5.2) 
DETERMINATION OF DURABILITY 


D-0 GENERAL 
D-0.1 Outline of the Method 


The durability of the material is determined by 
ascertaining actual behaviour of suitably prepared test 
panels in normal outdoor exposure test for a specified 
period and evaluating the results of the exposure by a 
suitable method of rating for various characteristics of 
the film ofthe material. Apart from this, the material is 
also evaluated by an accelerated weathering test 
wherein a prepared panel is subjected to controlled 
exposure to heat, light and water in an artificial 
weathering apparatus. 


D-1 TEST PANELS 


D-1.1 The panels shall be mild steel plate and shall be 
prepared as prescribed in 2 of IS 101 (Part l/Sec 3). 
The back and edges of the panels shall be protected 
with two coats of a suitable paint. 


D-1.1.1 For the Outdoor Exposure Test 
Panels shall be of sizes 150 mm x 100 mm x 1.25 mm. 
D-1.1.2 For the Accelerated Weathering Test 


Panels shall be preferably of sizes 130 mm x 40 mm x 
1.25 mm for UV-condensation type apparatus. 
However, panels may be of any other sizes suitable for 
accommodating in those apparatus. 


D-2 PREPARATION OF TEST PANELS 


D-2.1 In the painting procedure outlined under D-2.2, 
the air-drying of the films shall be done at room 
temperature and at a relative humidity of not more than 
70 percent. 


D-2.2 Thesurface ofthe test panels to be exposed shall 
be prepared as follows: 


a) Apply uniformly one coat of black japan by 
brushing to give a dry film mass of 17 to 
22 g/m? in accordance with 101(Part 3/Sec 4) 
and allow to air-dry for 48 h. 

b) Rub down lightly with smooth waterproof 
emery paper No. 280/320, wipe offthe surface 
using a piece of clean and dry soft cloth and 
then apply uniformly a second coat of the 
material and allow to air-dry. 

c) After air-drying for 2 days, force-dry the panel 
at 100? to 105?C in the oven for 4 h. Cool and 
subject to exposure test as in D-3.1. 


D-3 NORMAL OUTDOOR EXPOSURE TEST 


D-3.0 Subject the samples for registration and the 
tender samples, if supplied, to normal outdoor exposure 
test in the manner described under D-3.1. 


D-3.1 Expose in the open the test panels, prepared in 
the manner prescribed under D-1 and D-2 in duplicate 


IS 341 : 2016 


in a vertical position facing south. Commence the 
exposure not earlier than the third week of January and 
not later than the first week of April. 


D-3.1.1 Examine the condition of the exposed films 
at monthly intervals for the following characteristics: 


a) Gloss; 

b) Blackness; 

c) Checking, cracking and flaking; 
d) Chalking; and 

e) Spotting. 


D-3.1.2 For the above examinations, wash the right 
hand half of the surface of the two test panels by pouring 
water and then wiping with a soft cloth or chamois 
leather (see IS 1017). Adequate time for cooling of the 
panels to room temperature shall be allowed prior to 
washing examine the same half of the test panels at 
each examination. As an aid in the examination, a 
magnifying glass may be used, but the evaluation shall 
be based on an assessment with the unaided eye. At the 
end of the stipulated period for durability test, examine 
the two halves of the test panels. The sample shall be 
considered satisfactory if the material surface 
underneath as well as condition of the film in both the 
halves, the one washed periodically as well as the one 
washed only for the final examination is satisfactory 
by the method of evaluation described in G-3.2. Stray 
film failure, due to extraneous causes other than climate, 
shall be ignored. 


D-3.2 Rating and Evaluation of Film 


Characteristics of Test Panel 


The test panels before and after the specified periods 
of exposure tests shall be assessed for the various film 
characteristics as prescribed in D-3.2.1 and D-3.2.2. 


D-3.2.1 Method of Rating 


The film of an unexposed test panel shall be rated with 
the following basic values for the respective 
characteristics: 


a) Possessing high gloss and blackness 10 
b) Possessing correct or normal blackness 20 
c) Freedom from checking and cracking 30 


d) Freedom from chalking 20 
e) Freedom from spotting 20 
100 


NOTE —The initial rating of film may be 100 or less according 
to the condition of gloss and blackness, the rating for freedom 
from checking and cracking, chalking and spotting being always 
the maximum in the case of unexposed films. 


D-3.2.2 Evaluation of Exposed Films 


In recording the condition of exposed films at each 
examination, express the observed relative values of 
different characteristics in percentages of the basic 
value allotted to each characteristic under D-3.2.1. The 
allotment of performance values in col 4 of Table 2 
shall be in multiples of 10. For arriving at an assessment, 
multiply the basic value for each characteristic 
(see D-3.2.1) by the percentage awarded by the 
performance in the test and divide the product so 
obtained by 100 to obtain the percentage award for the 
observed value of each characteristic. Take the sum 
total of these resulting values as the overall assessment. 


D-3.2.2.1 Table 2 is intended to serve as an example 
for the assessment of a film of black japan after 
exposure. 


D-3.2.3 Results of Exposure 


Reckon the period for the general breakdown of the 
exposed Film from the date of commencement of 
exposure to the time when the overall assessment falls 
below 50 percent or when the performance value of 
any one characteristic falls below 25 percent of the basic 
value adopted for that characteristic. In the example 
given under G-3.2.2.1, though the overall assessment 
is 52.0 percent, yet the film is to be regarded as having 
generally broken down, because the performance value 
of chalking has fallen below 25 percent of its basic 
value. 


Table 2 Example of Reporting Evaluation of Exposed Films 
( Clauses D-3.2.2 and D-3.2.2.1 ) 


SI Characteristic Basic Value Performance Value, Assessment Value, 
No. Percent of Basic Value Computed from 

Performance Value 
(1) (2) (3) (4) (5) 
i) Possessing high gloss 10 50 5 
ii) Possessing correct colour 20 60 12 
iii) Freedom from checking and cracking 30 50 15 
iv) Freedom from chalking 20 20 4 
v) Freedom from spotting 20 80 16 
Total 52 


D-4 ACCELERATED WEATHERING TEST 


D-4.1 Accelerated Weathering Apparatus 


An artificial weathering apparatus of UV condensation 
type with following test condition parameters. 


a) Lamp Type : UV 313 

b) Test Cycle: UV — 4hat60+3°C 
Condensation —4hat50+3°C 

c) Irradiance : 0.67 


NOTE — For details of method of tests for UV apparatus follow 
6 of IS 101 (Part 6 /Sec 5). 


D-4.2 Preparation of Test Panels 
The test panels shall be prepared as given in D-1 


IS 341 : 2016 


and D-2. 


D-4.3 Procedure 


Sample for registration shall be tested in duplicate in 
the accelerated weathering apparatus (see D-4.1) and 
samples drawn from bulk supply shall be tested in a 
similar manner. Performance assessment will be done 
after exposure of 15 days using methods given in D-3.1 
to D-3.4. 


D-4.4 Observations 


The requirements of this test shall be taken to have 
been satisfied, if the performance of the film is not 
materially different as compared with the record of the 
film of the registered sample. 


ANNEX E 
[Table 1, SI No. (vi)] 
STRIPPINGTEST 


E-0 OUTLINE OF THE METHOD 

E-0.1 The minimum load required to produce a scratch 
showing the bare metal surface of the panel painted 
with the material is determined. 

E-1 APPARATUS 

The apparatus used for determining scratch hardness as 
prescribed in 3.2.2 of IS 101 (Part 5/Sec 2) shall be used. 
E-2 PREPARATION OF TEST PANELS 


E-2.1 Preparea tin panel as described in 7.1.5, 7.1.5.1 
and 7.1.5.2. 


E-3 PROCEDURE 


E-3.1 Testthe dried film in the apparatus under such a 
load that a scratch is produced showing the bare metal 
surface. 


E-4 OBSERVATIONS 


E-4.1 The material shall be deemed to have passed 
the test when the scratch so produced shall be free from 
jagged edges. 


IS 341 : 2016 


ANNEX F 
[Table 1, SI No. (vii)] 
DETERMINATION OF RESISTANCE TO KEROSENE 


F-0 OUTLINE OF THE METHOD 


F-0.1 The painted panels, after specified drying period, 
is dipped in kerosene at specified temperature and time. 
On completion of the time periods, the panels are 
subjected for visual examination. 


F-1 PREPARATION OF TEST PANELS 
F-1.1 Prepare a mild steel panel as described in 7.1.4. 


F-2 PROCEDURE 


F-2.1 Protect the edges of the panel by applying a coat 
of wax. Allow the panel to air-dry in a horizontal position 
for 96 h under room temperature in the laboratory 
conditions. Unless otherwise agreed, the panel then shall 
be conditioned at a temperature of 27° + 2°C and a 
relative humidity of 65 + 5 percent for a minimum of 16 
h. The test shall then be carried out as soon as possible. 


F-3 REAGENT 
F-3.1 Kerosene — Conforming to IS 1459. 


F-4 PROCEDURE 


F-4.1 Place sufficient amount of kerosene in a suitable 
vessel to completely or partially immerse the test panel. 
Immerse three-fourth of the test panel in the kerosene 
solution in an approximately vertical position using 
suitable supports, 1f necessary. Cover the container for 
the duration ofthe test to minimize the loss of reagent 
by evaporation or splashing. Keep the panel in this 
position in for 5 min at a temperature of 38°C. Remove 
the panel and wipe the immersed portion with a soft 
rag. Wash in running fresh water and allow to dry for 
1h. 


F-5 OBSERVATIONS 


F-5.1 Examine the immersed portion of the film for 
softening or deterioration. The material shall be deemed 
to have passed the test when the film shall not show 
any sign of softening or deterioration resulting in its 
removal when rubbed with a soft rag. 


ANNEX G 
[Table 1, SI No. (viii)] 
DETERMINATION OF RESISTANCE TO HEAT 


G-1 BLISTERING AND CRACKING 


G-1.1 Apparatus 


A drying-cum-heating oven of range up to 300?C of 
least count 2?C. 


G-1.2 Preparation of Test Panels 


Prepare mild steel panel of sizes 150 mm x 100 mm x 
1.25 mm as prescribed in 2 of IS 101 (Part 1/Sec 3). 
Apply a coat of black Japan uniformly on each side of 
the panel by brushing to give a dry film mass of 27 to 
34 g/m? in accordance with 101 (Part 3/Sec 4). 


G-1.3 Procedure 


Allow the panel to air-dry in a vertical position for 48 
h in a well ventilated room at room temperature. 
Illuminate the painted surface by diffused daylight for 
atleast 8 h during the drying period. Force-dry at 100? 


to 105°C for 1 h in the oven. Heat the panel to 230°C 
in a vertical position raising the temperature gradually 
at the rate of 3?C to 4?C per minute and maintain this 
for one hour. Cool to room temperature. 


G-1.4 Observations 


The material shall be deemed to have passed the test 
when the film shall not show any signs of running, 
blistering, cracking or other defects. 


G-2 TACKINESS 


G-2.1 Preparation of Test Panels 


Prepare mild steel panel of sizes 150 mm x 100 mm x 
1.25 mm as prescribed in 2 of IS 101 (Part 1/Sec 3). 
Apply a coat of Black Japan uniformly on each side of 
the panel by brushing to give a dry film mass of 27 to 
34 g/m? in accordance with 101(Part 3/Sec 4). 


G-2.2 Procedure 


G-2.2.1 Allow the panel to air-dry in a vertical position 
for 48 h in a well ventilated room at room temperature. 
Illuminate the painted surface by diffused daylight for 
at least 8 h during the drying period. Force-dry at 100° 
to 105°C for 1 h in the oven. 


G-2.2.2 Superimpose a second glass panel of about 
the same size as in G-2.1 on the painted side of the 
first panel and apply a load of 1 000 g placing a piece 


IS 341 : 2016 


of heat insulating material between the load and the 
glass. Heat the system for 1 h at 230?C. Cool to room 
temperature and separate the panels. 


G-2.3 Observations 


The material shall be deemed to have passed the test 
when the film of the material shall be free from visible 
damage and also shall not become tacky. The unpainted 
panel also shall be free from paint. 


Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods 
and attending to connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form 
without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of 
implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. 
Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. 

Review of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 


‘BIS Catalogue’ and ‘Standards : Monthly Additions’. 


This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.: CHD 20 (2074).
